chapter.title: Electrical Machinery and Equipment and Parts Thereof; Sound Recorders and Reproducers, Television Image and Sound Recorders and Reproducers, and Parts and Accessories of Such Articles

page.h1: HTS Chapter 85: Electrical Machinery and Equipment and Parts Thereof; Sound Recorders and Reproducers, Television Image and Sound Recorders and Reproducers, and Parts and Accessories of Such Articles — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: U.S. Electrical Machinery Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs (HTS Ch. 85) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What the EU, China, Canada, Mexico and other top buyers charge on U.S. electrical machinery, electronics and semiconductors, and what it takes to sell there.
keywords: electrical machinery export tariffs by country

intro: Tariffs decide very little of where this chapter's goods can go: four of the nine largest markets (Mexico, the EU, Hong Kong and South Korea) charge nothing, Malaysia and Taiwan charge 0% on chips and most electronics, Canada charges nothing on most goods but 25%–50% on a list of U.S. phones, network gear, monitors, appliances, parts and cable since September 2026, and China's own underlying rate on most electronics is already zero under the WTO Information Technology Agreement — only its flat 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods adds cost there. What usually decides access instead is a safety or radio-equipment approval (CE marking, CCC, KC, UKCA and similar schemes below) and, for the chapter's most advanced chips and chipmaking tools, U.S. export-control licensing rather than any foreign tariff — covered on the Export rules page.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

assumptions: Rates are grouped into two clusters per market rather than priced line by line: an "electronics" cluster (headings 8517–8542 covering phones, network gear, storage media, displays, cameras and semiconductors) that is largely covered by the WTO Information Technology Agreement and typically duty-free even outside a U.S. free-trade agreement, and an "electromechanical" cluster (motors, generators, batteries, appliances, switchgear and cable) that sees each market's ordinary, non-zero MFN rate. One representative subheading per cluster was checked for each non-FTA market; national 8–10-digit lines can differ from the representative rate.

For USMCA and KORUS partners (Mexico, Canada, South Korea), and for Hong Kong's duty-free port, the rate shown applies across the whole chapter, except for the lines on Canada's September 2026 counter-tariff list, which are named in the affected headings.

For the EU, Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 zeroes out the chapter from July 1, 2026; before that date the EU's own MFN rate was already 0% on the electronics cluster and a low single-digit rate on the rest.
China's 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods (in force since May 2025) is added on top of China's own MFN rate for every heading in this chapter; it is not specific to electronics.

For Taiwan, only the electronics cluster rests on a confirmed basis (its WTO Information Technology Agreement commitments); its rates on the other headings were not checked line by line and are marked as not individually verified.
